name: Dumbarton

attributes.attribute: fortress on a two-peaked basalt rock northwest of Glasgow
Koch name for the Dumbarton rock fortress, capital of Strathclyde

sources: Straffon, Cheryl. The Earth Goddess: Celtic and Pagan Legacy of the Landscape. London: Blandford, 1997, 172.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dumbarton sits on a huge two-peaked basalt rock northwest of Glasgow. The rock has been a fortress since prehistory. One legend marks it as the site of St. Patrick's objection to Roman soldiers trying to enslave part of his congregation. Another tale says witches threw stones at St. Patrick to drive him from Scotland. Those stones formed the rock. Rock-casting tales are also told of the Cailleach. Koch calls the site Alt Clut, or Dun Breatann. The fortress stands at the confluence of the River Leven and the River Clyde. It was sacked in 756 and served as the capital of Strathclyde.
